eyebrow: Done well, this rules something out for everyone

steps.label: Rule out mundane explanations first
steps.sub: undertuned LR, too few seeds, a bug -- those are fixes, not findings

steps.label: "Doesn't work" vs. "couldn't get it to work"
steps.sub: name explicitly what wasn't ruled out in the narrower claim

steps.label: Frame it as a hypothesis ruled out
steps.sub: not as time lost -- that's what makes it worth reading

eyebrow: A negative result stated with the same rigor as a positive one
code:
Negative result: Replacing standard attention softmax with a learned
temperature per head did not improve validation loss
(baseline: 2.341 ± 0.018, treatment: 2.337 ± 0.021, 4 seeds,
LR swept 0.5x-2x baseline for both). Difference is within noise.
caption: Same seed count, same LR-sweep discipline, same uncertainty reporting as any positive claim -- that's what makes it trustworthy.

eyebrow: Naming the narrower, honest claim explicitly
code:
We were unable to get sparse MoE routing to beat the dense baseline
at this scale within our compute budget (2 GPU-days).
We did NOT sweep expert count beyond {4, 8} -- a wider sweep or
larger scale may change this. We DID rule out LR and seed variance.
caption: "Couldn't get it to work" names what's unresolved -- a stronger, vaguer claim like "this doesn't work" hasn't earned that yet.
